subject: Computer mouse
title: Descent of the computer mouse
question: How did a wooden box with two wheels learn to roll, to see, and to feel?

ancestors.title: X-Y position indicator for a display system
ancestors.name: Engelbart position indicator
ancestors.trait: Two wheels at right angles under a hand-held box, one for X and one for Y, each turning a potentiometer
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 2/3: housing 26 on base 28, wheel 42 on shaft 44 to potentiometer 38, wheel 52 on shaft 48 to potentiometer 40, at right angles; keys 22 on top, glide 54, cord 18 (Fig. 1).

ancestors.title: Position indicator for a display system
ancestors.name: Rider ball mouse
ancestors.trait: One ball through the base replaces the wheels; small pick-off wheels read its roll
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 2: ball 8 through base 18 of the hemispherical housing 22, pick-off wheels 26 and 28 on hangers 31, 33 from plate 20, idler 24 on top of the ball, key 14, feet 36, 38; cord 9 (Fig. 1).

ancestors.title: Electronic mouse
ancestors.name: Kirsch optical mouse
ancestors.trait: No moving parts: a light source and a photodetector look at a spot on a patterned surface
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1/2: housing 14 with light source 17 and detector 21 (photocell 25) slanted to the spot 23 on the gridded surface 13; wall 27, bottom 31/33.

ancestors.title: Roller mouse for implementing scrolling in windows applications
ancestors.name: Gillick roller mouse
ancestors.trait: A roller between the two keys, turned by a finger, scrolls the window
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1: mouse 10, keys 18 and 22 either side of piece 20, roller 24 between them, side slot 25, top 26; Fig. 5: roller 24 on axle 36 in frame 30 over switch 35/37 on springs 29.

ancestors.title: Ambidextrous mouse
ancestors.name: Apple ambidextrous mouse
ancestors.trait: No keys: touch-sensitive zones under a smooth shell sense where the fingers are
ancestors.evidence: Fig. 1: mouse 20, housing 22, base 24, top member 26, touch-sensitive regions 28A, 28B and 28C (dashed); front-page figure: sensor nodes 188 and finger contact patches 196.
